title: How Layoff News Is Hiding a Hot Job Market

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即使在黑胶唱片时代，我还在夜店当DJ的时候，你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，然后你把DJ台

sentences.en: into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times,
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔维尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: American tech companies are slashing jobs dramatically, raising worries about a broader ripple effect.
sentences.zh: 美国科技公司正在大幅裁员，引发了人们对更广泛连锁反应的担忧。

sentences.en: I spoke to my colleague Gina Smilak about what's going on in the job market and what it tells us about this very strange time in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我和同事吉娜·斯米拉克聊了聊就业市场的现状，以及它向我们揭示了美国当前这个非常奇怪的时期。

sentences.en: economy.
sentences.zh: 经济方面。

sentences.en: It's Monday, December 12th.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月12日，星期一。

sentences.en: So you are our resident expert on the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你是我们常驻的美国经济专家，

sentences.en: economy, and we are very, very happy to have you back on the show.
sentences.zh: 我们非常、非常高兴你能回到节目中来。

sentences.en: Hopefully, you're happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 希望你也很高兴能来。

sentences.en: I am happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能来。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So we here at The Daily have been noticing lots of news about layoffs in the tech sector.
sentences.zh: 我们《每日新闻》注意到科技行业有很多裁员的消息。

sentences.en: You know, companies like Meta and Twitter said they'd be cutting jobs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，像Meta和Twitter这样的公司说他们要裁员。

sentences.en: Google and Amazon have announced they're putting a freeze on any new hiring.
sentences.zh: 谷歌和亚马逊也宣布暂停招聘新员工。

sentences.en: So my first question for you is this.
sentences.zh: 所以我给你的第一个问题是：

sentences.en: Are tech layoffs a sign of things to come?
sentences.zh: 科技行业的裁员是未来趋势的预兆吗？

sentences.en: Like, are they the opening bell of the bad news we've all been bracing for in the economy?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，它们是我们一直在经济中担心的坏消息的开端吗？

sentences.en: So in a word, I would say no.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，我会说不是。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The tech sector is, you know, clearly something worth watching, but it's a pretty unique part of our economy, and it's a very small one.
sentences.zh: 科技行业显然值得关注，但它只是我们经济中一个非常独特且规模很小的部分。

sentences.en: What's unique about the tech sector?
sentences.zh: 科技行业有什么独特之处？

sentences.en: Like, why is it not really that representative?
sentences.zh: 为什么它不那么具有代表性？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, I think it's important to think about how many people the sector actually employs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我认为考虑该行业实际雇佣了多少人很重要。

sentences.en: So those Meta layoffs that you mentioned, they were big, but they were about 11,000 people.
sentences.zh: 你提到的Meta裁员规模很大，但大约是11000人。

sentences.en: The Twitter layoffs were 3,750, give or take a few.
sentences.zh: Twitter裁员了3750人左右。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: In the economy, there are 153.5 million jobs.
sentences.zh: 整个经济体中有1.535亿个工作岗位。

sentences.en: So we're talking about a very small portion of the economy.
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈论的是经济中非常小的一部分。

sentences.en: Okay, drop in bucket.
sentences.zh: 好的，沧海一粟。

sentences.en: Tech as a whole makes up about 2% of jobs in the economy, so very small relative to the rest of the American workforce.
sentences.zh: 科技行业整体约占经济中工作岗位的2%，相对于美国其余的劳动力来说非常小。

sentences.en: And tech moves in weird ways in relation to stock markets.
sentences.zh: 而且科技行业与股市的关系很奇怪。

sentences.en: Weird how?
sentences.zh: 怎么个奇怪法？

sentences.en: Tech companies are very sensitive to what's happening in the economy and what is happening in markets.
sentences.zh: 科技公司对经济和市场发生的事情非常敏感。

sentences.en: And this is actually pretty common sense.
sentences.zh: 这其实是常识。

sentences.en: So people look for returns on their investments.
sentences.zh: 人们寻求投资回报。

sentences.en: And when they don't have a lot of good, safe alternatives to earn those returns, they tend to turn to tech companies, which are often sort of predicated on this idea
sentences.zh: 当他们没有太多好的、安全的替代方案来获得这些回报时，他们往往会转向科技公司，这些公司通常基于一种理念，

sentences.en: that they're going to make money down the road.
sentences.zh: 即他们未来会赚钱。

sentences.en: So this is a good benefit for them most of the time in a normal, healthy economy because people will actually give them financing more cheaply than they might otherwise
sentences.zh: 在正常、健康的经济中，这对他们来说大部分时间都是个好处，因为人们实际上会以比平时更低的成本为他们提供融资，

sentences.en: based on this belief that they're going to do well in the future.
sentences.zh: 基于他们未来会表现良好的信念。

sentences.en: They're going to make big earnings in the future.
sentences.zh: 他们未来会获得巨额收益。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, when things are less certain and when you see markets really fall off a cliff, in those moments, it becomes a lot more expensive
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，当情况变得不那么确定，当你看到市场真的跌入谷底时，在那些时刻，

sentences.en: for tech to finance those kinds of expansions.
sentences.zh: 科技公司为这种扩张融资的成本会变得高得多。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: You know, investors don't want to put their money at risk.
sentences.zh: 你知道，投资者不想让他们的钱处于风险之中。

sentences.en: They want shore bets only.
sentences.zh: 他们只想要稳赚不赔的买卖。

sentences.en: And in this cycle in particular, interest rates have gone up quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 特别是在这个周期中，利率上升了不少。

sentences.en: So they have safe places where they can put their money and they don't have to use these speculative investments to really earn that return.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有安全的地方可以存放资金，而不必利用这些投机性投资来获得回报。

sentences.en: And so what we've seen is it's become more expensive for tech companies to borrow and that can really change the calculus when they're looking at whether they want to expand,
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到的是，科技公司的借贷成本变高了，这在他们考虑是否要扩张、

sentences.en: whether they want to pursue a new project.
sentences.zh: 是否要开展新项目时，真的会改变计算方式。

sentences.en: And ultimately, all of that boils down to whether they want to hire people.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，这一切都取决于他们是否想雇人。

sentences.en: So it's more expensive to do new projects and expand and it's more expensive to hire, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，开展新项目和扩张的成本更高了，雇人的成本也更高了。

sentences.en: And so that's why you see tech tending to be very responsive to sort of the business cycle.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你会看到科技行业往往对商业周期非常敏感。

sentences.en: When things look uncertain and when rates rise unexpectedly and especially when investments like stocks sort of become less attractive,
sentences.zh: 当情况看起来不确定，当利率意外上升，尤其是当股票等投资变得不那么吸引人时，

sentences.en: you can really see these companies begin to pull back.
sentences.zh: 你真的可以看到这些公司开始收缩。

sentences.en: That makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这说得通。

sentences.en: Basically, when times get tough, investors pull their money out of tech companies.
sentences.zh: 基本上，当困难时期到来时，投资者会从科技公司撤资。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Gina, what about our own industry, media?
sentences.zh: 吉娜，我们自己的行业——媒体呢？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm also seeing headlines there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我也在媒体上看到了头条新闻。

sentences.en: Lots of layoffs, right?
sentences.zh: 有很多裁员，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, isn't that some sort of sign?
sentences.zh: 那难道不是某种信号吗？

sentences.en: Again, super tiny sector, not a big part of the broader economy and very sensitive to the advertising cycle.
sentences.zh: 同样，这是一个超级小的行业，不是更广泛经济的重要组成部分，而且对广告周期非常敏感。

sentences.en: Advertising is one of those sort of extra things in a company's budget where if they think that the economy might not be so solid next year, they're likely to pull back on.
sentences.zh: 广告是公司预算中那些额外开支之一，如果他们认为明年经济可能不太稳固，他们很可能会削减广告支出。

sentences.en: And so we have seen advertising spending down sharply and that results in media layoffs.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到广告支出大幅下降，这导致了媒体裁员。

sentences.en: Not necessarily a canary in the coal mine.
sentences.zh: 这不一定是煤矿里的金丝雀。

sentences.en: You know, it could be, but I think it's way too soon to say that it is.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它可能是，但我认为现在说它是还为时过早。

sentences.en: And you're saying we're pretty small.
sentences.zh: 你是说我们规模很小。

sentences.en: We're very small.
sentences.zh: 我们非常小。

sentences.en: We're very tiny in the sort of broader pie that is the American economy.
sentences.zh: 在美国经济这个大蛋糕中，我们非常微小。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Good for that ego check.
sentences.zh: 这对自我认知很有帮助。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: So the tech sector is unique.
sentences.zh: 所以科技行业很独特。

sentences.en: So is media.
sentences.zh: 媒体也是如此。

sentences.en: What is the broader job market like right now?
sentences.zh: 现在的就业市场整体情况如何？

sentences.en: So we are actually seeing continued strength in the broader economy.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们看到更广泛的经济持续走强。

sentences.en: Sort of the big story is a very resilient job market that seemed to just be chugging through all of this uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 大背景是一个非常有韧性的就业市场，似乎正在克服所有这些不确定性。

sentences.en: Layoffs are extremely low.
sentences.zh: 裁员人数极低。

sentences.en: Job openings are extremely high.
sentences.zh: 职位空缺极高。

sentences.en: There's about 1.7 jobs open in the country for every unemployed worker.
sentences.zh: 全国每有一个失业工人，就有大约1.7个职位空缺。

sentences.en: So just a very high level of job openings.
sentences.zh: 所以职位空缺水平非常高。

sentences.en: And unemployment is just hovering near a 50-year low.
sentences.zh: 失业率徘徊在50年来的最低点附近。

sentences.en: Wages are growing at the fastest pace in decades.
sentences.zh: 工资增长速度是几十年来最快的。

sentences.en: Overall, just a very solid hiring sort of picture right now.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，目前的招聘情况非常稳健。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So number one, that's really surprising.
sentences.zh: 第一，这真的很令人惊讶。

sentences.en: You know, this understanding that the economy is actually really hot right now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种对经济实际上非常火热的理解。

sentences.en: And number two, now that I know it is, what is the nature of its hotness?
sentences.zh: 第二，既然我知道它很火热，那么这种火热的本质是什么？

sentences.en: Like, which industries are doing well?
sentences.zh: 哪些行业表现良好？

sentences.en: Like, what's happening out there?
sentences.zh: 外面发生了什么？

sentences.en: So you see this strength across a bunch of different sectors in the economy.
sentences.zh: 你可以在经济的许多不同部门看到这种力量。

sentences.en: But I think one that's important to spotlight because it's just so strong is leisure and hospitality.
sentences.zh: 但我认为有一个行业值得重点关注，因为它非常强劲，那就是休闲和酒店业。

sentences.en: So these are the jobs that sort of do the services we interact with when we're on a trip.
sentences.zh: 这些工作就是我们在旅行时与之互动的服务。

sentences.en: Think hotel clerks, restaurant servers,
sentences.zh: 想想酒店职员、餐厅服务员，

sentences.en: you know, everyone you interact with at the airport, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是你在机场与之互动的每一个人。

sentences.en: These jobs are just going gangbusters.
sentences.zh: 这些工作正在蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: This industry is still hiring very quickly.
sentences.zh: 这个行业仍在非常迅速地招聘。

sentences.en: And it still has really solid wage growth, which is a sign that people are still competing for workers.
sentences.zh: 而且它仍然有非常稳健的工资增长，这表明人们仍在争夺工人。

sentences.en: You know, they want to hire and they're struggling to do so.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们想雇人，但却很吃力。

sentences.en: And so they're offering to pay more to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们愿意支付更高的薪水来做到这一点。

sentences.en: So restaurants, hotels out there competing for workers.
sentences.zh: 所以餐厅、酒店都在争夺工人。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So we're seeing that very strongly.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到这种情况非常强烈。

sentences.en: And remind me, Gina, what portion of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 提醒我一下，吉娜，休闲和酒店业大约占美国

sentences.en: labor force approximately is leisure and hospitality?
sentences.zh: 劳动力的多少？

sentences.en: Give me a minute.
sentences.zh: 给我一分钟。

sentences.en: I need to do the math.
sentences.zh: 我需要算一下。

sentences.en: It's 10.4% of the economy.
sentences.zh: 它占经济的10.4%。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: So it's a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以规模很大。

sentences.en: Yeah, so five times as big as the tech sector, basically.
sentences.zh: 是的，基本上是科技行业的五倍大。

sentences.en: Some other industries are also doing really well that are a little bit more surprising.
sentences.zh: 其他一些行业也表现得非常好，这有点令人惊讶。

sentences.en: You know, construction is continuing to hire really rapidly.
sentences.zh: 你知道，建筑业仍在非常迅速地招聘。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That's a bit of a surprise, a little bit of a head scratcher there, because as we all know, the housing market is really starting to pull back.
sentences.zh: 这有点令人惊讶，有点让人摸不着头脑，因为众所周知，房地产市场真的开始回落了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it seems like there's just so much construction already in that pipeline that people are still looking for workers where they can find them.
sentences.zh: 但似乎在建的项目太多了，人们仍然在寻找工人。

sentences.en: Interesting, because there's a lot of pent-up demand there.
sentences.zh: 有趣，因为那里有大量的压抑需求。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's pent-up demand.
sentences.zh: 这是压抑的需求。

sentences.en: Another place where we're seeing that is manufacturing continues to hire.
sentences.zh: 我们看到这种情况的另一个地方是制造业仍在招聘。

sentences.en: Most economists think that will slow down, but it hasn't really sort of fallen off a cliff yet.
sentences.zh: 大多数经济学家认为这会放缓，但它还没有真正跌入谷底。

sentences.en: So these are like car plants, and what are some examples of manufacturing?
sentences.zh: 所以这些就像汽车工厂，制造业还有哪些例子？

sentences.en: So we actually know, based on the government data, specifically where these manufacturing workers are being added, and it's really across a range of different jobs.
sentences.zh: 根据政府数据，我们实际上知道这些制造业工人被增加到了哪里，它确实涵盖了一系列不同的工作。

sentences.en: You know, we're seeing machinery manufacturers still hiring.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们看到机械制造商仍在招聘。

sentences.en: We're seeing continued hiring and sort of motor vehicle production.
sentences.zh: 我们看到机动车生产方面的持续招聘。

sentences.en: So it does seem like it's kind of pretty much across the economy.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来它几乎遍及整个经济。

sentences.en: We're still seeing pretty solid demand for these workers.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然看到对这些工人的需求相当稳健。

sentences.en: And then we're seeing decent demand still for some high-skill jobs.
sentences.zh: 然后我们看到对一些高技能工作的需求仍然不错。

sentences.en: So the information industry, which, you know, what is that?
sentences.zh: 所以信息产业，你知道，那是什么？

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: It's an industry that includes a lot of sort of complicated, more sort of high-education requirement kind of jobs.
sentences.zh: 这是一个包含许多复杂、对教育要求更高的工作的行业。

sentences.en: So think publishing industries,
sentences.zh: 所以想想出版业、

sentences.en: broadcasting, telecommunications, data processing.
sentences.zh: 广播、电信、数据处理。

sentences.en: We're still seeing some, you know, increases in that sort of segment of the economy, which is, you know, again, given the headlines we've been seeing, somewhat of a surprise.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然看到经济中这一领域有所增长，这再次考虑到我们看到的头条新闻，有点令人惊讶。

sentences.en: OK, so this all sounds really good, right?
sentences.zh: 好的，所以这一切听起来都很棒，对吧？

sentences.en: Like the job market is roaring.
sentences.zh: 就像就业市场正在蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: So we're done.
sentences.zh: 所以我们结束了。

sentences.en: Podcast finished.
sentences.zh: 播客结束了。

sentences.en: Podcast not finished.
sentences.zh: 播客还没结束。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: It's not that simple.
sentences.zh: 事情没那么简单。

sentences.en: You know, we all like having a hot labor market.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们都喜欢火热的劳动力市场。

sentences.en: It's great to have a hot labor market, that it is possible for the labor market to be too hot.
sentences.zh: 拥有火热的劳动力市场固然很好，但劳动力市场也有可能过热。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 我将在纽约市的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance,
sentences.zh: 万斯、

sentences.en: Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.zh: 齐尔兰·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无保留、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》APP进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: So, Gina, you just told us that the job market can sometimes actually be too hot.
sentences.zh: 那么，吉娜，你刚才告诉我们，就业市场有时确实会过热。

sentences.en: So explain that.
sentences.zh: 能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So this all comes back to inflation, which, as listeners on the show know, is a real problem in America right now.
sentences.zh: 这都要归结于通货膨胀，正如节目的听众所知，这是美国目前的一个真正问题。

sentences.en: The big I word.
sentences.zh: 那个以I开头的重大词汇。

sentences.en: The big I word.
sentences.zh: 那个以I开头的重大词汇。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a problem around the world.
sentences.zh: 没错，这是全球性的问题。

sentences.en: It's a problem here.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们这里的问题。

sentences.en: So we have had
sentences.zh: 所以我们经历了

sentences.en: 7.7% inflation over the past year.
sentences.zh: 过去一年7.7%的通胀率。

sentences.en: It's very rapid compared to normal, which is around 2%.
sentences.zh: 与通常约2%的水平相比，这非常快。

sentences.en: And while the job market wasn't the primary driver of inflation, with a job market this strong, it will be hard for inflation to come back down to that normal
sentences.zh: 虽然就业市场不是通胀的主要驱动因素，但就业市场如此强劲，通胀将很难回落到那个正常的

sentences.en: 2% level.
sentences.zh: 2%水平。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: There are kind of two big reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 这主要有两个大原因。

sentences.en: The first is wage growth.
sentences.zh: 首先是工资增长。

sentences.en: So when there are way more jobs open than there are available workers, companies pay more to hire.
sentences.zh: 当空缺职位远多于可用工人时，公司为了招聘会支付更多薪水。

sentences.en: They try and lure people away from their competitors.
sentences.zh: 他们试图从竞争对手那里挖人。

sentences.en: And as they pay more, as their labor bills go up, they charge more to try and cover those increasing costs.
sentences.zh: 随着他们支付更多薪水，劳动力成本上升，他们就会提高价格以试图覆盖这些不断增加的成本。

sentences.en: And so, you know, inflation is price increases.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，通货膨胀就是价格上涨。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so this can help to perpetuate price increases.
sentences.zh: 因此，这有助于使价格上涨持续下去。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The second mechanism here is when you, as a worker, are earning more, when your job prospects are solid and you're really doing well in the labor market,
sentences.zh: 第二个机制是，当你作为一名员工赚得更多，当你的工作前景稳固且你在劳动力市场表现确实很好时，

sentences.en: you're likely to spend more.
sentences.zh: 你很可能会花更多的钱。

sentences.en: You know, and as we all spend more, it's giving companies the wherewithal to keep charging more.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们都花得更多时，这给了公司继续涨价的财力。

sentences.en: And so, this sort of two-part relationship plays out when a job market is hot like it is right now that can keep inflation elevated.
sentences.zh: 所以，当就业市场像现在这样火热时，这种双重关系就会发挥作用，从而使通胀保持在高位。

sentences.en: So, this is kind of a double whammy for the inflation problem.
sentences.zh: 所以，这对通胀问题来说是一种双重打击。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is a big part of the inflation problem.
sentences.zh: 这是通胀问题的一个重要组成部分。

sentences.en: And, you know, I cover the Federal Reserve.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我报道美联储。

sentences.en: I spend all of my time thinking about what they're thinking about.
sentences.zh: 我把所有时间都花在思考他们正在思考的问题上。

sentences.en: And this is the number one thing they are thinking about right now.
sentences.zh: 而这是他们目前最关注的事情。

sentences.en: They are very aware of this and very concentrated on what comes next in the labor market.
sentences.zh: 他们非常清楚这一点，也非常专注于劳动力市场的下一步走势。

sentences.en: And Gina, going back to what you just mentioned before, spending, you know, people spending.
sentences.zh: 吉娜，回到你刚才提到的消费，你知道，人们的消费。

sentences.en: Is that happening?
sentences.zh: 这种情况正在发生吗？

sentences.en: What's happening with spending right now?
sentences.zh: 现在的消费情况如何？

sentences.en: What's really interesting is that spending had pulled back somewhat over sort of the late summer period.
sentences.zh: 真正有趣的是，消费在夏末期间有所回落。

sentences.en: And it seems to be re-accelerating a little bit right now.
sentences.zh: 而现在似乎又在小幅加速。

sentences.en: October consumer spending just out shows the biggest gain since June.
sentences.zh: 刚刚公布的十月份消费者支出显示了自六月以来的最大增幅。

sentences.en: We saw really good spending data in the sort of last personal consumption expenditures report.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一份个人消费支出报告中看到了非常好的消费数据。

sentences.en: Strongly expected consumer spending.
sentences.zh: 强劲的预期消费者支出。

sentences.en: It was up roughly twice what it was expected to be.
sentences.zh: 它比预期高出约两倍。

sentences.en: It's one of the very closely watched reports that just kind of tells us how the American consumer is doing.
sentences.zh: 这是最受关注的报告之一，它告诉我们美国消费者的状况如何。

sentences.en: And it looks like right now the American consumer is doing pretty well.
sentences.zh: 看起来目前美国消费者的表现相当不错。

sentences.en: How is this holiday season shaping up?
sentences.zh: 这个假期季表现如何？

sentences.en: How does it compare to previous years?
sentences.zh: 与往年相比如何？

sentences.en: The holiday weekend is off to a multi-billion dollar bang.
sentences.zh: 假期周末以数十亿美元的开局火爆开启。

sentences.en: And then I think we had that reinforced by some of the numbers we saw out of
sentences.zh: 我认为我们从以下数据中得到了印证：

sentences.en: Black Friday.
sentences.zh: 黑色星期五。

sentences.en: Retailers report nearly 200 million people flocked to stores from
sentences.zh: 零售商报告称，从感恩节到

sentences.en: Thanksgiving through
sentences.zh: 感恩节

sentences.en: Cyber Monday.
sentences.zh: 网络星期一，有近2亿人涌入商店。

sentences.en: That's 20 million more than a year ago.
sentences.zh: 这比一年前多了2000万人。

sentences.en: Black Friday online sales topped nine billion dollars for the first time.
sentences.zh: 黑色星期五在线销售额首次突破90亿美元。

sentences.en: We hit a new record on spending.
sentences.zh: 我们创下了消费新纪录。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So more than last year.
sentences.zh: 所以比去年多。

sentences.en: More than last year by a considerable margin.
sentences.zh: 比去年多出相当大的幅度。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I think that we have seen the consumer be really resilient.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为我们已经看到消费者非常有韧性。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: So where are people getting that money?
sentences.zh: 那么人们从哪里得到这些钱呢？

sentences.en: Like, is this money from these jobs that they have and they're really confident about?
sentences.zh: 这些钱是来自他们拥有的工作，并且他们对此非常有信心吗？

sentences.en: Or is this something else?
sentences.zh: 还是其他原因？

sentences.en: So a lot of it is coming from these jobs.
sentences.zh: 很大一部分来自这些工作。

sentences.en: People are getting hired.
sentences.zh: 人们正在被录用。

sentences.en: They're getting raises.
sentences.zh: 他们正在获得加薪。

sentences.en: They're working a lot of hours.
sentences.zh: 他们工作时间很长。

sentences.en: And that is helping them try to keep up with this fast inflation.
sentences.zh: 这正在帮助他们努力跟上这种快速的通货膨胀。

sentences.en: But the other thing is people are sitting on a lot of money from the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但另一件事是，人们在疫情期间存了很多钱。

sentences.en: You know, people got stuck at home.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们被困在家里。

sentences.en: They got stimulus checks.
sentences.zh: 他们收到了刺激支票。

sentences.en: And a lot of folks paid down their credit card debt.
sentences.zh: 很多人偿还了信用卡债务。

sentences.en: And so people are in good financial shape right now.
sentences.zh: 所以人们现在的财务状况很好。

sentences.en: Fed data shows that sort of across the board we're sitting on about $1.7 trillion in extra savings compared to what we would have expected relative to before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 美联储的数据显示，与疫情前相比，我们普遍拥有约1.7万亿美元的额外储蓄。

sentences.en: $1.3 trillion of that is in the top half of earners and about
sentences.zh: 其中1.3万亿美元在收入最高的一半人群手中，约

sentences.en: $350 billion.
So a smaller amount but still a sizable amount is sitting with the bottom half of earners who are much more likely to spend money out of savings.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然金额较小，但对于收入较低的一半人群来说，这仍然是一笔可观的数额，他们更有可能动用储蓄进行消费。

sentences.en: And like that's not normal, right?
sentences.zh: 这不正常，对吧？

sentences.en: Like this is kind of an odd effect of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这算是疫情的一种奇怪影响。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is not normal at all.
sentences.zh: 是的，这完全不正常。

sentences.en: This is a lot of savings and we've really seen people consuming out of them.
sentences.zh: 这是一大笔储蓄，我们确实看到人们正在消耗它们。

sentences.en: They're using this to sort of fuel their spending and keep up the consumption that they've gotten pretty used to over the last couple of years.
sentences.zh: 他们正在利用这些钱来推动消费，并维持他们过去几年已经习惯的消费水平。

sentences.en: And I think it ties back very much to the strong labor market story that we're telling.
sentences.zh: 我认为这与我们所说的强劲劳动力市场的故事有很大关系。

sentences.en: You know, people say very mean things about the economy when you ask them in surveys.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你在调查中询问人们时，他们对经济的评价非常刻薄。

sentences.en: They're not feeling good about it.
sentences.zh: 他们感觉不好。

sentences.en: They're not confident.
sentences.zh: 他们没有信心。

sentences.en: They're not happy.
sentences.zh: 他们不开心。

sentences.en: But then when you ask them how they feel about their own job prospects, they often strike a much more optimistic tone.
sentences.zh: 但当你问他们对自己工作前景的看法时，他们往往会表现出更乐观的态度。

sentences.en: And we're seeing in sort of the New York
sentences.zh: 我们以我喜欢关注的纽约

sentences.en: Fed survey, for example, which is one that I like to follow, we're seeing people feel pretty good about their future wage growth prospects.
sentences.zh: 联储调查为例，我们看到人们对未来的工资增长前景感觉相当不错。

sentences.en: And so I think, you know, even if you think that the economy is not chugging along the way you would like to see, at the end of the day, if you personally are getting, you
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，你知道，即使你认为经济没有按照你希望的方式发展，但归根结底，如果你个人正在获得

sentences.en: know, raises and your job is looking good and you feel like you could leave for a better job if you wanted to, you're
sentences.zh: 加薪，工作看起来不错，并且觉得如果愿意的话可以跳槽到更好的工作，你

sentences.en: pretty sour about the economy, but in real life when it comes to their own prospects in their own job, they're pretty happy.
sentences.zh: 对经济感到不满，但在现实生活中，谈到自己的工作前景时，他们相当高兴。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's where we are right now.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这就是我们目前的处境。

sentences.en: We're in this moment that is pretty good for workers, but they're also seeing their purchasing power rapidly eroded by inflation.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于一个对工人来说相当不错的时刻，但他们也看到自己的购买力被通胀迅速侵蚀。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this whole sort of constellation of developments is very bad for the Fed, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然，这一系列的发展对美联储来说非常糟糕。

sentences.en: I think a good way to think about it is this is good in the short term for workers because they're seeing good opportunities and good wage growth.
sentences.zh: 我认为一个很好的思考方式是，这对工人来说短期内是好事，因为他们看到了良好的机会和工资增长。

sentences.en: But it's potentially bad for them in the longer term because they're combating these very rapidly rising prices and there are a lot of reasons to think that this economy
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看，这对他们来说可能是不利的，因为他们正在对抗这些飞速上涨的价格，而且有很多理由认为这个经济

sentences.en: is going to have to slow down in order for inflation to moderate and that could be a very painful process for
sentences.zh: 将不得不放缓以使通胀温和化，这对

sentences.en: American employees.
sentences.zh: 美国员工来说可能是一个非常痛苦的过程。

sentences.en: So in other words, there's this tension between, on the one hand, good job security that exists across the economy right now and on the other, keeping prices low, getting
sentences.zh: 换句话说，一方面是目前整个经济中存在的良好就业保障，另一方面是保持低物价、降低

sentences.en: inflation down.
sentences.zh: 通胀，这两者之间存在张力。

sentences.en: those two things are in conflict.
sentences.zh: 这两件事是冲突的。

sentences.en: There is definitely a tension and I think we've kind of been in the rising action phase of that tension all year long and we're now about to hit sort of the climax of that tension.
sentences.zh: 确实存在张力，我认为我们整年都处于这种张力的上升阶段，现在我们即将达到这种张力的顶点。

sentences.en: We're sort of on this precipice where things are really going to get decided.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于一个悬崖边上，事情真的要见分晓了。

sentences.en: How this all plays out is really going to be determined in 2023.
sentences.zh: 这一切如何发展将在2023年决定。

sentences.en: And what's going to happen,
sentences.zh: 会发生什么呢，

sentences.en: Gina?
sentences.zh: 吉娜？

sentences.en: What's your crystal ball say?
sentences.zh: 你的水晶球怎么说？

sentences.en: So nobody knows because the economy is always weird and hard to predict, but it is super weird and hard to predict right now.
sentences.zh: 没人知道，因为经济总是很奇怪且难以预测，但现在它超级奇怪且难以预测。

sentences.en: But I think that based on what we do know now, economists are kind of expecting two basic potential outcomes.
sentences.zh: 但我认为基于我们现在所知道的，经济学家们正在期待两种基本的潜在结果。

sentences.en: I think there's a really bad scenario, which is sometimes referred to as the hard landing scenario.
sentences.zh: 我认为有一个非常糟糕的情景，有时被称为硬着陆情景。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, when we talk about a bad scenario for the economy, the trends we're seeing now could potentially make it worse.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，当我们谈论经济的糟糕情景时，我们现在看到的趋势可能会使情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: In a hard landing, inflation doesn't come down as quickly as the
sentences.zh: 在硬着陆中，通胀下降的速度没有达到

sentences.en: Fed is hoping.
sentences.zh: 美联储的预期。

sentences.en: You have a Fed that has to get even more aggressive in trying to slow down the economy in order to wrangle those price increases.
sentences.zh: 美联储必须在试图减缓经济以控制这些价格上涨方面变得更加激进。

sentences.en: So it's raising rates, raising rates, raising rates.
sentences.zh: 所以它在不断加息、加息、加息。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I think in this scenario, you get a
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在这种情景下，你会得到一个

sentences.en: Fed that gets into
sentences.zh: 进入2023年的美联储，

sentences.en: 2023, looks around, sees that the labor market is still just chugging along, consumer spending is chugging along, and there's so much momentum that it kind of needs to tap
sentences.zh: 环顾四周，看到劳动力市场仍在稳步前进，消费者支出也在稳步前进，而且势头如此强劲，以至于它需要更用力地踩下

sentences.en: those brakes harder to get it to stop.
sentences.zh: 刹车才能让它停下来。

sentences.en: Because inflation is still out of control.
sentences.zh: 因为通胀仍然失控。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think in that scenario, the real risk is that you've got a Fed that sort of puts those brakes on at the same time as people start to run out of those savings
sentences.zh: 我认为在这种情景下，真正的风险在于美联储在人们开始耗尽我们一直在谈论的那些储蓄

sentences.en: buffers that we've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 缓冲的同时踩下了刹车。

sentences.en: All of this hits the economy at the same time or over the same time period because monetary policy takes a while to really play through the economy, and you could get a pretty
sentences.zh: 所有这些都在同一时间或同一时期冲击经济，因为货币政策需要一段时间才能真正传导到经济中，你可能会经历一场相当

sentences.en: painful recession where people lose a lot of jobs.
sentences.zh: 痛苦的衰退，人们会失去很多工作。

sentences.en: And so there is a very potentially negative outcome, that could still happen, but we're not going to know until, you know, a little bit into next year.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常潜在的负面结果，它仍然可能发生，但我们直到明年某个时候才会知道。

sentences.en: And what's the good scenario?
sentences.zh: 那理想的情况是什么样的？

sentences.en: In the good scenario, inflation might come down perhaps gradually, but pretty solidly, and the job market will cool down, but it won't crash.
sentences.zh: 在理想情况下，通胀可能会逐渐但相当稳健地下降，就业市场会降温，但不会崩溃。

sentences.en: There are a couple of things about today's economy that make you think that that's possible.
sentences.zh: 当今经济中有几点迹象让你觉得这是可能的。

sentences.en: One, inflation is going to moderate for a bunch of different reasons from supply chain healing to sort of the return of car production that should help inflation come down.
sentences.zh: 第一，通胀将因多种原因而放缓，从供应链的修复到汽车生产的恢复，这些都应有助于通胀下降。

sentences.en: All those job openings we talked about earlier could give the labor market this nice room for adjustment where employers can just sort of stop hiring rather than
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到的所有职位空缺，可能会为劳动力市场提供一个很好的调整空间，雇主可以停止招聘，而不是

sentences.en: laying all of their workers off.
sentences.zh: 解雇所有的员工。

sentences.en: And maybe it's the case that consumers, because they have such good balance sheets already, you know, just kind of spend down their savings, stop spending, and inflation kind of
sentences.zh: 也许消费者因为资产负债表状况良好，会消耗掉他们的积蓄，停止消费，通胀就会以一种

sentences.en: fades in this very benign, easy way that we haven't seen in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我们过去从未见过的非常温和、轻松的方式消退。

sentences.en: Like it's not an emergency, not really a recession even.
sentences.zh: 就像这不是一场紧急情况，甚至算不上真正的衰退。

sentences.en: Some would call it a soft landing.
sentences.zh: 有些人会称之为“软着陆”。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay, you economists.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你们这些经济学家。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we have this soft landing, this very optimistic scenario, where you see a sort of gradual slowdown next year.
